question: What backup scope does Veeam Agent for Oracle Solaris need so that I can do a bare metal recovery from recovery media later?
gold_facts: Bare metal recovery with Veeam Recovery Media requires a backup that includes the full contents of the root directory.
Set the --includedirs option to / when creating the job (e.g. veeamconfig job create ... --includedirs /).
A job with this scope generates an additional configuration file needed for bare metal recovery.

A.text: For bare metal recovery, the backup must include the full contents of the root directory [1]. Bare metal recovery is only supported from file-level backups created by version 4.0.0.1029 (or later) of Veeam Agent for Oracle Solaris [2]. Note that backups created from within a non-global zone cannot be used for bare metal recovery, because they do not contain the required system metadata file [4].

documents.title: Before You Begin
documents.text:
[Before You Begin › Before You Begin]
Before You Begin
================

Before you boot from the recovery image and restore your data, review the following prerequisites and considerations:


* You must have a recovery image on any media from which your machine can boot: CD/DVD/BD, removable storage device or virtual CD/DVD drive.

* To restore the system and data, you must have both Veeam Recovery Media and data backup. Make sure that the backup is available on the machine drive (local or external), on a network shared folder or on the backup repository managed by a Veeam backup server.


Performing bare metal recovery requires a backup that includes the full contents of the root directory. To configure a job for such backup, set the value of the \-\-includedirs option to /. For details, see [Creating Backup Jobs](backup_job_create.html).


* The media type on which you have created the recovery image must be set as a primary boot source on the machine.

* The backup from which you plan to restore data must be successfully created at least once.

* \[For backups stored in network shared folders or in Veeam backup repositories] You must have access to the target location where the backup file resides.

* \[For Veeam backup repository targets] If you plan to restore data from a backup stored in a Veeam backup repository, you must have permissions to access that backup repository. To learn more, see [Setting Up User Permissions on Backup Repositories](integrate_permissions.html).

* When you restore data with Veeam Recovery Media, Veeam Agent for Oracle Solaris restores backup content directly to the available disks of the recovered system and replaces the current disk content.

* Review [consideration and limitations](backup_job_acl.html#considerations) for restoring ACLs.


Navigating Veeam Recovery Media Menu and Wizards

In the Veeam Recovery Media wizard, the use of mouse is not supported. To navigate the wizard and associated dialog windows, you can use the following keys:


* Tab — to switch between displayed controls in the working area and buttons in the buttons area. The currently selected control or button is highlighted with green color.
* Up and Down — to switch between items in a scrollable list.
* Space — to select the necessary item in a list. The selected item's check mark may vary in different steps of the wizard.

* Enter — to proceed to the next step of the wizard or to open a directory.

* Escape — to return to the previous step of the wizard or to exit the wizard if you are in the main menu.

documents.title: Bare Metal Recovery
documents.text:
[Bare Metal Recovery › Bare Metal Recovery]
Bare Metal Recovery
===================

If the operating system on your machine fails to start, you can perform bare metal recovery of your system. To do this, you must have Veeam Recovery Media that you created on your functional system and a full backup with system metadata. 


At the first stage of bare metal recovery, you must boot your machine from Veeam Recovery Media which launches the recovery image OS in your machine RAM. You then import the backup file into the Veeam Agent database and run the restore. Veeam Agent erases all data on the machine, reconstructs partition structure using system metadata, restores data from the backup and creates the boot loader. 


Before you reboot the machine upon successful bare metal recovery, you may need to restore additional data from another backup. To do this, you can use the standard file\-level restore functionality. Veeam Agent mounts the backup file to the file system of the recovery image OS. After that, you can copy the necessary files or directories to a desired location.


Considerations and Limitations for Bare Metal Recovery

* Bare metal recovery to dissimilar hardware is not supported.
* Bare metal recovery of SVM configurations is not supported.
* Bare metal recovery from backups created from within non\-global zones is not supported.
* Bare metal recovery only from file\-level backups created by version 4\.0\.0\.1029 (or later) of Veeam Agent for Oracle Solaris is supported.

* Bare metal recovery requires a backup that includes the full contents of the root directory (the \-\-includedirs option must be set to /).
* Paths longer than 1006 symbols cannot be restored during bare metal recovery and must be restored manually afterwards.

* Bare metal recovery supports file system encryption keysource: "raw,ephemeral" and "passphrase,prompt". For file systems whose encryption has an different keysource, Veeam Agent will prompt to specify a passphrase to keep the encryption after restore.

* During bare metal recovery, Veeam Agent does not restore data from ZFS volumes.
* \[For flexible mapping] You cannot map a ZFS pool that resides on a disk slice.

* \[For flexible mapping] You cannot map the system rpool to multiple disks.

* \[For flexible mapping] Any special ZFS pool configurations, such as RAIDZ, mirroring, cache devices, and so on, are ignored. All the disks assigned to the source ZFS pool are simply added together to form the target ZFS pool.


* During bare metal recovery, access (atime), modified (mtime) and changed (ctime) timestamps are reset for all non\-empty files and directories.

Related Task

[Performing Bare Metal Recovery](baremetal.html)

documents.title: Zone Backup
documents.text:
[Zone Backup › Zone Backup]
Zone Backup
===========

You can use Veeam Agent for Oracle Solaris to back up data pertaining to individual non\-global zones configured in the Oracle Solaris OS. Veeam Agent offers two scenarios for zone backup.


Scenario 1: backup from the global zone

You can install Veeam Agent in the global zone and configure the backup job to include directories with files pertaining to a non\-global zone whose data you want to back up. 


This scenario has the following requirements:


* The root account of the global zone must have access to the file systems of the non\-global zone.
* The global zone must own the storage device that contains the file system of the zone.

If the global zone does not meet either of these requirements, use Scenario 2\.


| Zone Backup Note |
| --- |
| It is not required to stop the backed\-up zone before the backup process starts. To ensure consistency of the backed\-up data, you can use custom scripts, for example, to create a ZFS snapshot or UFS snapshot. To learn more about custom scripts, see [Backup Job Scripts](backup_job_script.html). |


Scenario 2: backup from a non\-global zone

You can install Veeam Agent in the non\-global zone whose data you want to back up and specify which files and directories to back up in the same way as in case you back up data of the global zone.


| Zone Backup Note |
| --- |
| * You must install the product license in each Veeam Agent installed in each non\-global zone. * You cannot use backups created from within a non\-global zone for bare metal recovery because such backups do not contain the required system metadata file. |

B.text: For bare metal recovery, the backup must include the full contents of the root directory — set the --includedirs option to / (e.g., veeamconfig job create --name system_backup --reponame [vbr01] --includedirs /). Such a backup job also generates an additional configuration file required for restoring files during bare metal recovery [1].

documents.title: Getting Started
documents.text:
Getting Started

To protect your machine from a disaster of any kind, you must perform the following operations in Veeam Agent for Oracle Solaris:

1. Create Custom Veeam Recovery Media.

Veeam Recovery Media provides an alternate way to boot your machine in the event of a disaster. If your machine fails to start or the hard disk gets corrupted, you can boot the Oracle Solaris OS from Veeam Recovery Media and restore your data. 

To learn more, see [Creating Veeam Recovery Media](recovery_media_create.html).

1. Define what data you want to back up and configure the backup job.

Before you configure the backup job, you should decide on the following backup details:

* Backup destination: where you want to store your backed\-up data.
* Backup scope: what directories and files you want to back up.

| Important |
| --- |
| [Performing bare metal recovery with Veeam Recovery Media](baremetal.html) requires a backup that includes the full contents of the root directory. To configure such backup job, set the value of the \-\-includedirs option to /, for example, veeamconfig job create \-\-name system\\ backup \-\-reponame \[vbr01] \-\-includedirs /. The backup job with such scope generates an additional configuration file required for restoring your files during bare metal recovery. |

* Backup schedule: how often you want to back up your data.

After that, you can configure one or several backup jobs. The backup job captures the data that you have added to the backup scope and creates a chain of restore points in the target location. If your data gets lost or corrupted, you can restore it from the necessary restore point.

To learn more, see [Performing Backup](backup_tasks.html).

1. Monitor backup task performance.

You can get information about backup and restore sessions status and view session logs. To learn more, see [Reporting](reporting.html).

1. In case of a disaster, you can restore data from a Veeam Agent backup. To learn more, see [Performing Restore](disaster_recovery.html).

question: The protected users count on my Veeam Data Cloud for Entra ID dashboard is higher than the licences I'm consuming. Why the difference?
gold_facts: The protected users count includes all existing users in the Entra ID tenant regardless of type or status.
Only enabled Entra ID member users count towards the license.

A.text:
The number of protected Entra ID users shown on the dashboard includes all existing users in your Microsoft Entra ID tenant, regardless of their type or status. This number may differ from the number of consumed licenses because only enabled Entra ID member users are counted towards the license [1][2].

In other words, licensing is based on the user accounts you back up: each enabled Entra ID member user counts towards your purchased license or free allowance, while groups, roles and other Microsoft Entra ID objects do not consume the license or allowance (though Veeam Data Cloud still protects them) [3][4]. Disabled and guest users are protected but do not consume your license or allowance [3].

Note also that users created before the userType attribute was introduced on August 31, 2014 have that value unset (null), and Veeam Data Cloud licenses and processes these accounts the same way as Entra ID member users [3][4].

documents.title: Viewing Dashboard
documents.text:
Viewing Dashboard

The Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft Entra ID dashboard contains information on the state of the protection of your Microsoft Entra ID tenant, the number of protected objects and the recent restore sessions.

To view the dashboard, do the following:

1. On the Entra ID page, click the name of the tenant you want to manage.
2. The dashboard is the landing page when you open a tenant. To return to the Entra ID tenant dashboard from a different page, click Dashboard.

The Dashboard page displays the following sections.

* The Protection Status section displays information on state of your Entra ID backups.
* The Objects Protected section displays information on the number of protected Entra ID objects.

| note |
| --- |
| The number of protected Entra ID users includes all existing users in your Microsoft Entra ID tenant, regardless of their type or status. This number may differ from the number of consumed licenses because only enabled Entra ID member users are counted towards the license. For details, see [Licensing](entra_id_licensing.html). |

* In the Recent Activity section, you can review the log of recent backup and restore sessions. Click View All Activity to display a complete log of activities. For details, see [Viewing Backup and Restore Sessions](entra_id_activity.html).

[

![Viewing Dashboard](/media/b3e6b6c8-21ae-4206-a24a-5087be68d412/400e1c02214e.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the Dashboard screen in Entra ID, showing Protection Status with a green shield indicating protection is turned on, Objects Protected with a donut chart totaling 358 objects, and Recent Activity listing successful backup sessions.

](images/entra_id_dashboard.png "Viewing Dashboard")

documents.title: Licensing
documents.text:
Licensing

Licensing for Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft Entra ID is based on the user accounts you back up. Each enabled Entra ID member user is counted towards your purchased license or free allowance. Groups, roles and other Microsoft Entra ID objects do not consume the license or allowance, but Veeam Data Cloud protects them too. Any additional users beyond the contract quantity are subject to overage charges.

If you reduce the number of enabled Entra ID member users in your Microsoft Entra ID tenant, Veeam Data Cloud will revoke their license usage after the next backup is complete.

| note |
| --- |
| In Entra ID, the type of the user account is specified by the value of the userType attribute (Member or Guest). Microsoft Entra ID users who were created before the introduction of the userType attribute on August 31, 2014, have this value unset (null). Veeam Data Cloud licenses and processes these user accounts the same way it licenses and processes Entra ID member users. |

Licensing Plans

To protect your Entra ID data, you can choose one of the following licensing plans depending on the Veeam Data Cloud subscriptions that you want to use. The Entra ID Standalone plan allows you to protect your Entra ID data only. If you also want to protect your Microsoft 365 data, you can choose one of the bundle plans.

The bundles include a free allowance for your Entra ID tenant. You can protect up to three enabled Entra ID member users for every backed\-up Microsoft 365 user. For example, if 10,000 Microsoft 365 licensed users are backed up in Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft 365, you can protect up to 30,000 enabled Entra ID member users in Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft Entra ID. Veeam Data Cloud also protects disabled and guest users, but they do not consume your license or allowance. Note that you can use the allowance only when all Microsoft 365 users in your Microsoft 365 tenant are backed up. For details, see [Veeam Data Cloud Fair Use Policy](https://www.veeam.com/legal/veeam-data-cloud-fair-use.html).

For more information on available licensing plans, see [Pricing and Plan Options](https://www.veeam.com/products/saas/microsoft-entra-id-backup-service.html?ad=menu-products-portfolio-test-a#pricing).

**Licensing Plans**

| Licensing Plan | Included Options | License Unit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft 365 Premium | Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft Entra IDVeeam Data Cloud for Microsoft 365 FoundationVeeam Data Cloud for Microsoft 365 Express | Microsoft 365 user |
| Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft 365 Advanced | Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft Entra IDVeeam Data Cloud for Microsoft 365 Foundation | Microsoft 365 user |
| Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft Entra ID Standalone | Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft Entra ID | Entra ID user |

License Expiration

If your subscription expires and you do not renew it, Veeam Data Cloud will suspend your backup policy for 30 days. During this period, your existing Entra ID backups are still available, and you can use Veeam Data Cloud to restore your Entra ID data. After 30 days, Veeam Data Cloud will permanently delete your Entra ID tenant and all related data.
